commentary: Market breadth sitting at 46.1% indicates underlying participation weakness across broad US equities, with less than half of the universe above long-term averages. Meanwhile, core Treasury bond ETFs (AGG, IEF, TLT) remain pinned below their 200-day moving averages as interest rate volatility persists, failing to deliver active positive hedging returns. The portfolio remains positioned with risk sleeve assets concentrated in strong momentum drivers (LITE, VLO, NVDA) and real assets (DBC) that remain well above their 200-day moving averages. The bond sleeve is maintained near its minimum floor to satisfy mandatory asset allocation rules without over-allocating capital to non-trending fixed income assets. A sustained market breadth expansion above 55% alongside Treasuries reclaiming their 200-day moving averages would trigger a reallocation toward broader market exposure.
allocation_reason: Target bond weight is set at 0.287, which sits 0.037 above the 0.250 minimum floor and 0.463 below the 0.750 maximum ceiling. This allocation maintains required fixed income presence while minimizing exposure to bond funds currently trading below their 200-day moving averages.
